blocks.x:
Chris is a Senior News Writer for Collider. He can be found in an IMAX screen, with his eyes watering and his ears bleeding for his own pleasure. He joined the news team in 2022 and accidentally fell upwards into a senior position despite his best efforts.
For reasons unknown, he enjoys analyzing box office receipts, giant sharks, and has become known as the go-to man for all things Bosch, Mission: Impossible and Christopher Nolan in Collider's news division. Recently, he found himself yeehawing along to the Dutton saga on the Yellowstone Ranch.
He is proficient in sarcasm, wit, Photoshop and working unfeasibly long hours. Amongst his passions sit the likes of the history of the Walt Disney Company, the construction of theme parks, steam trains and binge-watching Gilmore Girls with a coffee that is just hot enough to scald him.
His obsession with the Apple TV+ series Silo is the subject of mockery within the Senior News channel, where his feelings about Taylor Sheridan's work are enough to make his fellow writers roll their eyes.

Anya Taylor-Joy is having one hell of a year. She already has the first billion-dollar movie of 2026 under her belt, she's heading back to Arrakis before the year is out, and right now, three of her projects are finding big audiences at home at the same time.

The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, The Gorge and Lucky are all performing on streaming, giving Taylor-Joy three hits across film and television at once. Better still, she's got another movie coming to Netflix in a couple of weeks. Lucky has been a big one for Apple TV. The seven-part crime thriller debuted at No. 1 in the United States, knocking Silo out of the top spot, with Taylor-Joy starring as a con artist who thought she'd escaped her old life until her past comes looking for her again.

Then there's The Gorge, which has stuck around for a long time. Taylor-Joy stars opposite Miles Teller (Top Gun: Maverick) in the sci-fi action movie, which premiered on Apple TV in 2025 and has continued finding viewers well into 2026. And if that wasn't enough, there's The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. Taylor-Joy returned as Princess Peach for the animated sequel, which became the first movie released in 2026 to pass $1 billion at the worldwide box office before making the jump to home viewing.
Anya Taylor-Joy's Next Streaming Movie Is Already Coming

Taylor-Joy's next movie arrives on Netflix in just a couple of weeks, too, as she stars opposite Chris Evans in Sacrifice, which premieres on October 16. Taylor-Joy plays Joan, the leader of a group that storms a fancy charity gala on a Greek island and takes Evans' struggling movie star hostage, with their plan eventually involving taking him to an actual volcano, so things don't exactly improve from there.

Evans (Avengers: Endgame) and Taylor-Joy (Furiosa) lead a cast that also includes Vincent Cassel (Black Swan), Salma Hayek Pinault (House of Gucci), John Malkovich (Con Air), Sam Richardson (Veep), Ambika Mod (One Day), Charli XCX, and Yung Lean. Romain Gavras (Athena) directs the movie, which filmed across Greece, Bulgaria and Iceland, where they found an active volcano to throw Evans into.
Taylor-Joy also has Dune: Part Three arriving in theaters later this year. Sacrifice premieres on Netflix in the United States and France on October 16.
Jonathan Tropper, Cassie Pappas, Jonathan van Tulleken
A reformed con artist thinks she has finally outrun her old life, until a botched robbery and a winning lottery ticket she cannot safely cash put her back on the run.
